The later correction (the cancellation of the earlier R411A booking) is likewise recorded in the system log – the “cancel_flight_booking” response that confirmed the cancellation of confirmation B227DF – and appears as **m00012** in the public audit.  

Those two log entries together establish when the original purchase was made and when it was subsequently undone and replaced.  

What the public record does **not** contain is any explicit statement of the user’s permission to make the purchase. The permission (that Owen Park may travel on 2026‑12‑09, with no upgrades and a $370 budget) is only present in the user’s instruction text, not in the system‑generated logs. In other words, the public evidence shows the actions and their timestamps, but it lacks a publicly visible record of the authorization that allowed those actions.
